summary:
EmberSpotter is a web app that shows fire activity month by month, from 2001 to 2026, in a calendar of years and months. It joins MODIS (Terra and Aqua) and VIIRS NOAA-20 detections into one fair time series, so it doesn't matter anymore which sensor saw the fire.

You pick a region and a date range, and you get:

-=- A calendar heatmap with the harmonized fire counts for every month.
-=- How each month compares to its usual level (its historical median).
-=- The raw data next to the harmonized data, so you can see what the sensor change does.
-=- CSV downloads of the hotspots and the monthly series.
details:
We built EmberSpotter because comparing fire data over the years is harder than it looks. NASA has two satellite sensors that detect fires: MODIS since 2000 and VIIRS since 2018. VIIRS is much more sensitive, so if you just put both together it looks like fires suddenly exploded in 2018, which isn't true.

Our app fixes that. You pick any country, state or draw your own area anywhere in the world, and EmberSpotter converts the old MODIS data into what VIIRS would have seen. That gives you one fair fire history from 2001 to today. It also tells you how confident it is in the result, so you're not just trusting a number.

With it you can see the fire season, the worst years, whether this year is above or below normal, a monthly map, and download everything as CSV.

We made it with JavaScript, Leaflet and NASA FIRMS data, and it runs free on GitHub Pages. Right now the demo uses labeled sample data while we finish connecting the real FIRMS data.
